Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8350-dedupe-emptiness-trims`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

Unblocked: objectui#8175 / PR #8349 has landed on `main` (verified by content — `resolveNameField` now appears 3× in `record-details.tsx`), so the ladder this card is about is the two-candidate version, not the six-entry literal walk the card was filed against. **Re-read it on your own base.**

Two things this card's fix shape depends on, both binding:

- ⚠️ **Reuse `valueAt`'s definition; do not write a second trim.** One authority, not two implementations that happen to agree today — writing a parallel emptiness test recreates the very divergence this card exists to close, one level down.
- ⚠️ **The pin must assert the DEDUPE outcome** — which row renders and which drops, on a whitespace-only fixture — **not the title**. A title-only pin passes green while this stays wrong, because the two halves are decided in different packages. objectui#8175's harness `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/record-details.nameFieldDedupe-8175.test.tsx` is the shape, and note how it splits the two halves into separate `it()`s: inside one case the first failure short-circuits the second, so a combined case would redden the duplicate half and say nothing about the vanishing half.

Every negative needs a control that fires — "row absent" is trivially true on a document that rendered nothing.
